# A conjecture on a pro-nilpotent group generated by quantum-dilogarithm multiplets

*Self-contained statement (2026-08-11). Written to be readable without the rest of
this repository. Derivations, measurements and history are in
`s_leading_term_existence.md`; the harness is
`experiments/s_pronilpotent_conjecture.py`.*

> **The §3 consequence is now an engine on the canonical surface** (2026-08-12):
> `bps_factor_spectrum.py`, with the accessor
> `BPSKAlgebra.spectrum_generator_from_factors(cutoff)` and its cross-check
> `verify_spectrum_generator_from_factors`. It is the repo's **second** spec-free
> `S`-finder, and it covers what the first cannot: the peel recursion
> (`recursive_spectrum.py`) reattaches `E_𝖖(F_γ)` and so honest-fails on a
> character-charge node, putting N=2\*/Markov and the wild quivers out of reach,
> while this construction has no such gate. Measured on 18 quivers
> (`experiments/s_ray_spectrum_benchmark.py`): peel gates out on 4, rays build
> all 18, `S` agrees **exactly** on all 14 both build. On cost neither engine
> dominates and the variable is the **cone size**, not the rank: rays are faster at
> cone degree 2 (1.5–2.1×, rank 16–32), the peel engine is faster at degree ≥ 3 and
> rank ≥ 10 (1.1–1.7×) and at rank ≤ 4 (up to 3.9×), and only the factor engine builds
> at all wherever the gate trips. (An earlier "~3× at rank 12–24" reading of that
> benchmark was an artifact of a case mix whose high-rank entries were all at degree
> 2, so it measured degree rather than rank; retracted — `repo_audit.md` A46.)
> Because surjectivity below is conjectural, what the engine ships is a cross-check
> against an **independently computed** `S` (`verify_spectrum_generator_from_factors`,
> against the chart's own `_s_coefficient`), and the suite
> (`tests/test_ray_spectrum.py`) pins it against `S_from_spec`, the peel engine, and
> the prototype. `verify_leading_data` is by contrast *enforced by construction* — a
> regression guard on the arithmetic, not evidence about surjectivity
> (`repo_audit.md` A44). Reorganising the prototype for speed gave 37× overall and
> 634× at rank 16 — mostly from replacing a `(D+1)^rank` cone scan with the
> degree-`≤D` simplex.

## 1. Setup

Let `Γ` be a lattice with an antisymmetric integral form `⟨•,•⟩`, and let
`γ(1), …, γ(n) ∈ Γ` generate a **strict** (pointed) cone. Write `Γ⁺` for the
non-zero elements of the `ℤ_{≥0}`-span, equipped with an additive degree
`d : Γ⁺ → ℤ_{≥1}`. Fix a cutoff `D` and put `Γ⁺_D = {γ : d(γ) ≤ D}`, a finite set.

On the quantum torus `X_γ X_δ = 𝖖^{⟨γ,δ⟩} X_{γ+δ}` let

```
𝒢_D  =  1 + 𝔪 ,        𝔪 = ⊕_{γ ∈ Γ⁺_D} ℤ((𝖖))·X_γ ,
```

a nilpotent group (class bounded by `D` through the degree filtration); `𝒢 = lim← 𝒢_D`
is pro-nilpotent. This is the construction of Kontsevich–Soibelman's `G_V`
(*Stability structures, motivic Donaldson–Thomas invariants and cluster
transformations*, §1.4, §2.3), for the `Γ`-graded associative algebra taken to be the
quantum torus.

**Dictionary.** `𝖖` is Kontsevich–Soibelman's `q^{1/2}` (so `q = 𝖖²`), and

```
E_𝖖(x) = (−𝖖x; 𝖖²)_∞^{-1} = Σ_{n≥0} (−𝖖)^n x^n /(𝖖²;𝖖²)_n = ∏_{k≥0}(1 + 𝖖^{2k+1}x)^{-1}
```

is their `E(q^{1/2},x)` — the **bosonic** quantum dilogarithm — verified coefficient
by coefficient. Note `ord_𝖖(c_n) = n` exactly, where `c_n = (−𝖖)^n/(𝖖²;𝖖²)_n`.

## 2. The generators

For `γ ∈ Γ⁺` and `s ∈ ½ℤ_{≥0}`, with `j` running over `−s, −s+1, …, s` in integer
steps,

```
E^{(s)}_𝖖(X_γ)  =  ∏_{j=−s}^{s}  E_𝖖( (−1)^{2s} 𝖖^{2j} X_γ )^{(−1)^{2s}}
```

— so integer `s` gives even shifts `𝖖^{2j}` and factors `E_𝖖`, while half-integer `s`
gives odd shifts and *inverse* factors. Both signs are needed: the sign inside the
argument is forced (dropping it destroys the pure `SU(2)` spectrum), while the
exponent `(−1)^{2s}` does not change the group generated and only fixes the sign
convention for the multiplicities.

Write `ℰ(γ)` for the subgroup generated by the `E^{(s)}_𝖖(X_γ)`, `s ∈ ½ℤ_{≥0}`. Setting
`χ_s = 𝖖^{−2s} + 𝖖^{−2s+2} + ⋯ + 𝖖^{2s}` and

```
P = ℤ[𝖖, 𝖖^{-1}]^{pal}      (palindromic Laurent polynomials; the χ_s are a ℤ-basis)
```

the map `Ω = Σ_s a_s χ_s  ↦  A_γ(Ω) := ∏_s E^{(s)}_𝖖(X_γ)^{a_s}` is a group isomorphism
`P ≅ ℰ(γ)` (**Lemma 1**; all `X_{nγ}` commute, so the multiplets at `γ` commute and
their exponents add). Finally

```
ℰ  =  ⟨ ℰ(γ) : γ ∈ Γ⁺ ⟩  ⊆  𝒢 ,
```

which is defined without reference to any ordering.

## 3. The conjecture

> **Conjecture.** For every total order `σ` of `Γ⁺_D`, the multiplication map
> ```
> μ_σ :  ∏_{γ ∈ Γ⁺_D} ℰ(γ)  ⟶  ℰ_D ,        the product taken in σ-order,
> ```
> is a **bijection**. Equivalently: every element of `ℰ` factors as an ordered
> product of BPS factors, in **every** order, and uniquely.

Equivalently again, in the form in which it was first met: the set of ordered
products does not depend on the order.

**Consequence (the question this came from).** Prescribe arbitrary *leading data*
`t : Γ⁺ → ℤ`. Then there is a **unique** `S ∈ ℰ` whose coefficient at `X_γ` has no
`𝖖^{≤0}` part and has `𝖖^1`-coefficient `t(γ)`, for every `γ`; it is computed by a
degree-by-degree recursion in any order, and is order-independent. Taking
`t = −1` on the `γ(a)` and `0` elsewhere gives `S = 1 − 𝖖 Σ_a X_{γ(a)} + O(𝖖²)`.

## 4. What is proved, and what is not

| statement | status |
|---|---|
| `ℰ(γ) ≅ P`, so equal-charge letters merge (Lemma 1) | **proved** |
| `μ_σ` **injective** — the factorisation is unique | **proved**: the coefficient at `γ` is `f(lower data) − L·Ω_γ` with `L = 𝖖/(1−𝖖²)`, and `Ω ↦ −LΩ` is injective on `P` |
| `bar(A)A = 1` for every BPS factor, hence for any product in any order | **proved**: `bar(E_𝖖) = E_𝖖^{-1}`, and palindromy of the shift set repairs the shifted factors |
| `μ_σ` **surjective** | **conjectural**, already for a single `σ` |

Surjectivity follows from a single **pairwise** hypothesis, by a collection argument
(the orders form a finite symmetric group, generated by adjacent transpositions; a
swap costs a commutator whose charges have strictly larger degree, so words sort
modulo the degree filtration):

> **(C) — the exchange identity.** For all `γ, δ ∈ Γ⁺_D` and all
> `s, s' ∈ ½ℤ_{≥0}`,
> ```
> E^{(s)}_𝖖(X_γ) · E^{(s')}_𝖖(X_δ)  =  E^{(s')}_𝖖(X_δ) · ( a product of multiplets at the charges
>                                      iγ+jδ, i,j ≥ 1, in any order ) · E^{(s)}_𝖖(X_γ) .
> ```
> Equivalently `[ E^{(s)}_𝖖(X_γ), E^{(s')}_𝖖(X_δ) ] ∈ ⟨ ℰ(iγ+jδ) : i, j ≥ 1 ⟩`.

The exchange form carries two things the commutator form does not. It asserts that
the **outer factors return unchanged** — same charges, same spins — which is a
separate claim, and is measured below rather than assumed. And "in any order" for the
middle makes the identity **recursive**: every interior charge has degree
`≥ d(γ) + d(δ)`, so the middle product is a strictly smaller instance of the same
problem, and exchanging adjacent generators sorts any word by induction up the degree
filtration. That single two-generator identity is therefore all that reordering
needs.

Two remarks on the shape of (C).

**It suffices to test single multiplets, not general `Ω`.** The collection argument
only ever needs commutators of *generators*, and `ℰ(γ)` is generated by the `E^{(s)}_𝖖(X_γ)`;
a general `A_γ(Ω)` is a word in them, so if generator–generator commutators land in
the interior subgroup, every word sorts. (An earlier draft quantified (C) over all
pairs `Ω, Ω' ∈ P`, which is unnecessary.)

**Hence (C) is indexed by three integers.** Nothing about `γ` and `δ` enters except
their bracket, so the hypothesis is a family of rank-2 statements over

```
( ⟨γ,δ⟩ , s , s' )  ∈  ℤ × ½ℤ_{≥0} × ½ℤ_{≥0} ,
```

which is the whole conjecture reduced to a two-charge, three-parameter question.

(C) is also *necessary*, so it is equivalent to the conjecture.

**What is known about (C).** It is trivial when `⟨γ,δ⟩ = 0`. Its leading term is
known exactly and is integral: rescaling `Y_γ := L·X_γ` makes the structure constants
**quantum integers**,

```
[Y_γ, Y_δ] = −[⟨γ,δ⟩]_𝖖 · Y_{γ+δ} ,        [b]_𝖖 = (𝖖^b − 𝖖^{−b})/(𝖖 − 𝖖^{-1}) ,
```

so the commutator's leading term is `Ω Ω' ·(−[⟨γ,δ⟩]_𝖖)· Y_{γ+δ} ∈ P·Y_{γ+δ}`. The
commutator is moreover bar-unitary, which supplies the `𝖖 ↦ 𝖖^{-1}` anti-invariance
half of the required integrality for free.

**Where a proof must bite.** The missing half is *polynomiality*, and it cannot follow
from anti-invariance alone: `L_n = 𝖖^n/(1−𝖖^{2n})` satisfies `bar(L_n) = −L_n` for
every `n`, yet `L_n/L = 1/[n]_𝖖` is a Laurent polynomial only at `n = 1`. In the
`Y`-normalisation the log of a BPS factor is the multi-cover formula

```
log A_γ(Ω) = Σ_{n≥1} (−1)^n /(n·[n]_𝖖) · Ω^{(n)}(𝖖^n) · Y_{nγ}
```

(with `Ω^{(n)}` carrying `ε^{n+1}`, `ε = (−1)^{2s}`, so half-integer spin enters even
covers with a minus). A proof of (C) must show that the `n ≥ 2` terms — those carrying
the `n·[n]_𝖖` denominators — cancel. That places the whole difficulty at non-primitive
charges.

## 5. Relation to Kontsevich–Soibelman

Their `G_V` is the same construction, and their **Conjecture 1** — that decomposing
`T_{1,0}·T_{0,k}` in the opposite order yields integer exponents — is an integrality
statement of the same kind (a weak form is proved in Reineke, *Poisson automorphisms
and quiver moduli*). They also state the refined ansatz outright in
*Cohomological Hall algebra, exponential Hodge structures and motivic
Donaldson–Thomas invariants*: the motivic DT-series "admits an infinite product
expression in terms of standard `q`-special functions (basically, shifted quantum
dilogarithms) with integer exponents". Three differences remain:

1. **Orders.** They decompose in the clockwise and anti-clockwise orders — the orders
   a central charge realises. The conjecture above asks for **every** order, including
   those no central charge produces. This is not vacuous: at the pentagon with cutoff
   `5` a linear central charge gives 2 or 3 rays while free insertion gives 6, and the
   element is the same.
2. **The object.** They work with the whole pro-nilpotent group; the conjecture is
   about the **subgroup** generated by the multiplets, which is proper (the correction
   available at each charge is confined to `L·P`, while a general coefficient is
   arbitrary in `ℤ((𝖖))`).
3. **Packaging of integrality.** They decompose and conjecture the exponents come out
   integral; here membership in the integral palindromic lattice is *imposed* and the
   existence of the decomposition is conjectured.

Their categorical Factorization Property (proved, via Harder–Narasimhan-type
filtrations) gives the BPS factorization **in the phase order** — which is exactly the
case that was never in doubt; an arbitrary order has no filtration representing it.

## 6. Evidence

All arithmetic exact; the only truncation is along the positive cone, so every verdict
below is a statement about the truncated cone, not a proof.

* **The conjecture as stated** (`experiments/s_pronilpotent_conjecture.py`): on
  pentagon, Kronecker-2, Kronecker-3, the 3-cycles `(1,1,1)`, `(2,2,2)` (Markov) and
  `(3,3,3)`, and a random rank-5 quiver — `0` failures of Lemma 1, `0` of injectivity,
  `0` `Ω` outside `P`, `0` inexact reconstructions. The re-factorisations move the ray
  content (pentagon: 9, 11, 12 rays) while fixing the element.
* **The exchange identity directly**, in the form stated above and with the outer
  factors *required* to come back unchanged. `experiments/s_exchange_identity.py`:
  brackets `1…3`, `2s, 2s' ∈ {0,1,2,3}` — 48/48. Extended in
  `experiments/s_exchange_identity_extensive.py`:

  | axis | cases | orders each |
  |---|---:|---:|
  | brackets `−3…6` (negative included) × `2s, 2s' ≤ 4`, cutoff 4 | 225 | 4 |
  | cutoff 5, brackets `1…3`, `2s ≤ 2` | 27 | 3 |
  | cutoff 6, same | 27 | 3 |

  **0 failures** — about 1060 factorisations in all, outer factors recovered in every
  one, every interior multiplicity in `P`, every reconstruction exact. Control at
  bracket `0`: the two factors commute, so the middle must be **empty** — verified for
  all 25 spin pairs rather than passing vacuously. Off-lattice perturbation detected.

  **On "in any order":** the hypothesis needs only that *at least one* order of the
  middle works, since the others follow by the same recursion (user, 2026-08-11). The
  runs above are deliberately stronger — the interior charges are permuted at random
  and *every* permutation is required to work. That is extra evidence, and a failure
  there would not have falsified the conjecture.
* **The same hypothesis in commutator form** (`experiments/s_spin_grid_hypothesis.py`):
  bracket `0…3` against `2s, 2s' ∈ {0,1,2,3}` — **64/64**, with `b = 0` checked to give
  a *trivial* commutator and an off-lattice perturbation failing to factor.
* **(C) with general `Ω`** (superseded as a test by the grid, but consistent with it),
  brackets `0…4`, deterministic and random `Ω`: no pure-ray components, no `Ω` outside
  `P`, exact reconstruction.
* **Negative control**: perturbing an element by `𝖖⁰` off the `L·P` lattice must break
  the re-factorisation, and does.
* **Generic two-charge reordering** (`experiments/s_two_charge_reordering.py`), the
  most direct form of the statement: form `A_γ(Ω)·A_δ(Ω')` and refactor it in the
  opposite order (`δ` first, intermediate charges by slope, `γ` last). All 13 cases
  tried reorder — brackets `0…3`, with `Ω, Ω'` drawn from `1, 2, χ_{1/2}, χ_1, −1` —
  every multiplicity in `P`, every reconstruction exact. `b = 0` is the control
  (nothing appears in between); an off-lattice perturbation fails to reorder.
  At `Ω = Ω' = 1` this reproduces the familiar answers: the pentagon at `b = 1`, and
  at `b = 2` the `SU(2)` spectrum with `χ_{1/2}` at `(1,1)`.

  The multiplicity at the first intermediate charge is, in every case measured,

  ```
  Ω(γ+δ) = [⟨γ,δ⟩]_𝖖 · Ω · Ω'          (product in the ring P)
  ```

  **In the generating orientation only** — worth spelling out, since the setup here
  supplies it silently and a reader who lifts the formula out of it will get the
  wrong answer half the time. The refactorisation above deliberately reverses the
  pair (`δ` first, `γ` last), and the pentagon identity
  `E(X_a)E(X_b) = E(X_b)E(X_{a+b})E(X_a)` yields the interior factor in **one** order
  only: a pair already in the other order contributes **exactly `0`** at `γ+δ`.
  Swept across both orientations on random quivers (rank 2–16,
  `experiments/s_ray_spectrum_stress.py` battery B) the dichotomy is exact — the
  interior appears iff the order places `γ` after `δ` while `⟨γ,δ⟩ > 0` (or the
  mirror), the value is `[⟨γ,δ⟩]_𝖖·Ω·Ω'` there and `0` otherwise, and it is
  **never a third thing**: 171/171 generating, 163/163 flat, 69/69 at
  `⟨γ,δ⟩ = 0` (where the two commute and both orders must give nothing).

  e.g. `[3]·χ_{1/2}² = 𝖖^{-4}+3𝖖^{-2}+4+3𝖖²+𝖖⁴` at `b = 3, Ω = Ω' = χ_{1/2}`, exactly
  as measured. Two features worth noting: with `Ω = −1` the reordering still lands in
  `P` but the multiplicities go **negative**, so the lattice condition survives what
  positivity does not; and general `Ω` is strictly richer than the classical case —
  at `b = 1`, `Ω = Ω' = 1` gives the three-factor pentagon while `Ω = χ_{1/2}` gives
  seven factors with multiplets out to `(4,1)`.

* **Independently of the above**, order-independence of the recursion was measured on
  22 further collections (rank up to 6, degenerate forms, dependent and non-primitive
  charge sets, cutoffs to 7), on random quivers at rank 8, 12 and 16, and for
  *arbitrary* leading data — with `(f_σ − f_τ)/L` a palindromic element of `P` at
  every one of 375 charges checked.

### 6a. Stress test of 2026-08-13

Four batteries, added because the evidence above is deep in the *order* direction
and thin in the *quiver* direction, and because the one place a proof has to work
— the `n ≥ 2` multi-cover terms — had never been checked for whether the existing
coverage reaches it at all.

* **Across the whole BPS-quiver dictionary** (`experiments/s_ray_stress_dictionary.py`).
  All **1108** entries of `n_001 … n_008`, rank ≤ 8, each against its own
  spec-derived `S` (a Nahm-sum expansion sharing no code path with the recursion):
  1108/1108 on `S == oracle` **at every cone degree**, on `phase == lex ==
  degree-phase`, on cutoff nesting `D → D−1`, and on `Ω ∈ P`.  Repeated with
  *arbitrary* integer leading data — where no oracle applies but
  order-independence still must — same result.  Controls: the pentagon passes
  every column; a corrupted spec makes the oracle comparison fail, so it is not
  a blind comparison.

  **What that equality licenses, exactly.**  The build runs in a generic phase
  order, not the spec's.  So the inference "the spec chamber *is* the ray
  factorisation in its own order" chains three things, and only one of them is a
  theorem: order-independence (**measured**, on these same 1108 entries) moves
  the built element to the spec's order; injectivity (**proved**) then forces the
  multiplicities to agree with the spec's, given the elements agree
  (**measured**).  Stated as a conditional rather than a conclusion, because the
  first link is exactly what the conjecture is about.

* **The multi-cover regime, first asked and then pushed**
  (`experiments/s_ray_stress_multicover.py`).  §19 places the whole difficulty at
  non-primitive charges, so the battery first measures whether the exchange
  identity's interior ever *reaches* one: at cutoff 6, **33/36** parameter cells
  place content at a charge with `gcd(i,j) > 1`.  It does, so the coverage is not
  vacuous for the hard half.  Then the identity itself, past the previously
  measured envelope — brackets `7…10` and `−4…−6`, spins to `2s = 6`, cutoffs to
  7 — **102/102**, outer factors recovered every time.

  And the same cancellation in a case with an independent answer: **pure SU(2) in
  its weak-coupling chamber at cutoff 16** reproduces the known spectrum exactly
  (`Ω = 1` on the dyon tower, `χ_{1/2}` at `(1,1)`) with **zero** content at every
  multi-cover charge `(k,k)`, `k ≥ 2`.  Also the sharpest degenerate case:
  **rank 1** at cutoff 32, where there is no bracket anywhere to help — `Ω = 1` at
  `γ`, `0` at every `nγ`, and `S` equal to `E_𝖖(X_γ)` coefficient by coefficient.

* **Conjugation stability, isolated** (`experiments/s_ray_stress_conjugation.py`).
  The 2026-08-11 correction above splits (C) into a rank-2 rearrangement *and*
  stability of `⟨ℰ_interior⟩` under conjugation by the ray subgroups, but every
  measurement tests the conjunction.  This one conjugates a random interior word
  by `A_γ(Ω)` (inverse via Lemma 1, `A_γ(Ω)^{-1} = A_γ(−Ω)`, itself checked) and
  requires the result to re-factor into interior factors only — zero multiplicity
  forced onto either boundary ray.  Controls: Lemma 1; conjugation by the identity
  BPS factor; an off-lattice perturbation must fail to factor.

  **120 parameter cells, zero leakage** — brackets `−4 … 6`, cutoffs 4–6, `Ω`
  drawn from `P` up to `2s = 3`, conjugating at both `γ` and `δ`, with several
  random interior words and several random re-factorisation orders per cell.
  (Brackets 1–4 carry the full cutoff-6 depth; the wider brackets are measured at
  cutoffs 4–5, because the refactorisation cost at cutoff 6 with `2s = 3` runs to
  minutes per cell.)  So the half of (C) that had never been separated out does
  not fail anywhere measured — which means the exchange identity's evidence is
  not resting on one of its two halves silently carrying the other.

* **Free insertion, many quivers rather than many orders**
  (`experiments/s_ray_stress_free_orders.py`).  78 dictionary quivers × 4 fully
  shuffled orders on `S`: 78/78, factor content moving on 76/78.  And — since the
  conjecture is about *every* element of `𝓔`, not only the leading-data-pinned
  `S` — 58 quivers × 3 orders on **random ordered products of BPS factors**:
  58/58, content moving on 46/58.

* **Adversarial and structural** (`experiments/s_ray_stress_adversarial.py`).
  `bar(S)·S = 1` on 11 quivers × 2 orders (a *guard*, since it is provable for any
  ordered product — and not a membership test for `𝓔`, whose bar-unitary
  overgroup is strictly larger); the forced answers at zero pairing, zero leading
  data and `+1` leading data; ray-cache independence; the argument guards; and
  degenerate central charges (all-equal, near-tied, on the real axis, overflow
  scale) leaving `S` unchanged while the factor content moves 2 ↔ 13.  Five negative
  controls, each verified to bite — including the finding that the superseded
  `−𝖖·Ω` read is **blind** on pure SU(2) and the pentagon and only detectable on
  Kronecker-3 and Markov.

* **The DT identification against root systems**
  (`experiments/s_ray_stress_finite_type.py`).  On a finite-type quiver the
  spectrum should be hypermultiplets at positive roots; the recursion knows
  nothing of that and demonstrably *can* emit higher spin (checked first as a
  control, so the prediction is not vacuous).  Sampling central charges to reach
  the rich chambers — a single generic `Z` lands in the minimal chamber, where
  the statement is trivially true — over A₂–A₆, D₄–D₆, E₆, E₇: **zero**
  non-hypermultiplet content and **zero** content off a positive root, with
  A₂/A₃/A₄/A₆/D₄ recovering *all* of `Φ⁺`.

### 6b. Conjecture 1 on RANDOM elements of `𝓔`, at scale (2026-09-04)

The evidence in §6/§6a is overwhelmingly about **`S`**, and `S` is a very special
element of `𝓔`: its `Ω` are forced by the leading data, and on a physical chamber
they are mostly `1`.  Conjecture 1 is stated for *every* `g ∈ 𝓔`.  The one prior
battery on general elements — `s_ray_stress_free_orders.py --random-elements` —
covers 58 quivers × 3 orders, and its reach is set by its enumeration:
`FreeOrder` walks a `(D+1)^rank` **box**, so its own table caps the cone degree
at 3 by rank 5, and it samples `--per-file 12` entries from `n_002 … n_005`.
That leaves ranks 6–8 untouched for general elements, spin capped at `2s = 2`,
and `Ω` coefficients in `[−2, 2]`.

This campaign re-runs the question on the **cone simplex** (`C(D+r, r)` points,
the shape `bps_factor_spectrum.cone_simplex` uses) with its own exact
coefficient arithmetic — which is what lets it reach rank 8 and every entry.

**An independent implementation, deliberately.**  `experiments/pbw_e_group.py`
re-implements `Q_𝖖(Γ)`, the coefficient ring `Z[𝖖,𝖖⁻¹,(1−𝖖^{2n})⁻¹]`, `E_𝖖`,
`E^{(s)}_𝖖` and the read-off from scratch; it shares no code path with
`bps_factor_spectrum`, `recursive_spectrum` or `habiro`.  That is the point: on
the engine path integrality is *manufactured* by `_forced`, never measured
(`repo_audit.md` A44), so an engine agreeing with itself is not evidence.  It is
cross-checked against the engine in `experiments/pbw_controls.py` C7 — the
engine's own `Ω`, composed here in the **same** `piece_key` order, reproduce the
engine's `S` coefficient by coefficient inside the repo's ring
(`HabiroElement.__eq__`, exact algebraic equality) at pentagon / Kronecker-2 /
Kronecker-3 / 3-cycle(1,1,1).

**The test, stated exactly.**  The `x`-linear coefficient of `E^{(s)}_𝖖` is
`−𝖖·χ_s/(1−𝖖²)` (control C1, `2s = 0…8`).  A factor placed at `γ` contributes to
`X_γ` only at `γ`'s own cone degree, so at each degree `d` the element
`P_{<d}^{-1}·g` has, at each `γ` of degree `d`, coefficient
`Σ_s Ω(γ,s)·(−𝖖 χ_s/(1−𝖖²))`.  Hence

> `Ω(γ,·)` is integral  ⟺  that coefficient times `(1−𝖖²)/(−𝖖)` lies in `P`
> (integral **and** palindromic),

and two independent things can fail: a `(1−𝖖^{2n})` denominator with `n > 1` can
survive, or the residual can fail to be palindromic.  Both are checked, and the
rebuilt ordered product is then compared to `g` exactly.

This also makes the read-off well defined for an **arbitrary** total order, not
only a cone-compatible one: writing the ordered product as `U·(1+A)·V` with
`U, V` starting at `1` and `A` of degree exactly `d`, `U A V ≡ A` modulo degree
`> d`, so the placement of the degree-`d` factors cannot affect the degree-`d`
coefficients.  The order enters only through the arrangement of the
strictly-lower-degree factors inside `P_{<d}`.

**Controls (`experiments/pbw_controls.py`, 96/96).**  Positive: the linear
coefficient two ways; a single generator `E^{(s)}(X_γ)^{p}` factorizing to
exactly `{(γ,s): p}` for `p ∈ {1,−1,2,−3}` over four charges and four spins;
`bar(g) = g^{-1}` on random words; factorize→rebuild exact; the engine
cross-check above.  **Negative, which is what stops the battery being vacuous** —
the note's own example: `E_{𝖖²}(X_γ)` **is** bar-unitary and **must not**
factorize, and does not (a `(1−𝖖^{2n})` denominator survives at the first
charge); a `𝖖⁰` bump off the `L·P` lattice fails 3/3.  Plus a vacuity guard on
the order axis: the factor count must *move* between orders — on one pentagon
word it is 4 / 44 / 62 / 92 / 169 across anti-degree / shuffled / spin-first /
degree-lex / lex-reversed, for the same element.

**One defect found and fixed on the way, recorded because it is exactly the
failure mode this kind of harness produces.**  The coefficient representation
`num / ∏(1−𝖖^{2n})^{e}` is **not canonical** — `1/(1−𝖖²)` and `(1+𝖖²)/(1−𝖖⁴)`
are the same number with different `(num, den)`.  Reading integrality off the
representation (`den == {}`) therefore reports "not integral" for coefficients
that *are* Laurent polynomials: it **manufactures false counterexamples to the
conjecture**.  It must divide, not inspect.  Caught by controls C3/C4/C5a before
any sweep was run — which is the whole argument for running the negative
controls first.

#### The runs

Words of 5 generators (4 in the deep run), charges drawn from the low cone,
spins `2s ≤ 4` (5–6 in the deep and large-bracket runs), exponents in
`{±1, ±2, ±3}`; each word re-factorized in 6–7 total orders — degree-lex,
**anti-degree** (every top-degree factor before any node factor: reachable by no
central charge and by no degree-compatible scheme), lex-reversed, spin-first, and
2–3 fully shuffled orders of the truncated `Γ₊ × ½ℕ`.

| run | lattices | factorizations | max `2s` measured | result |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| dictionary `n_001 … n_008` (`pbw_dictionary_sweep.py`) | **1108** | **19 944** | 31 | 0 failures |
| the same, charges biased onto **non-primitive** `kγ`, `k ≥ 2` (`--nonprimitive`) | **1108** | **19 944** | 37 | 0 failures |
| deep cone at low rank (`D = 10/9/7/6` at rank 1/2/3/4), spin to `2s = 6` | 119 | 1 428 | 63 | 0 failures |
| **large brackets**, synthetic (`pbw_large_bracket_sweep.py`) | 69 | 1 932 | **91** | 0 failures |

**43 248 factorizations over 1 177 distinct lattices, zero failures.**

**Why the large-bracket run exists.**  Measured here: across all 1108 dictionary
entries every pairing entry lies in **`[−2, 2]`**.  So the dictionary sweep,
however broad in rank, does not probe large `⟨γ_i,γ_j⟩` at all — and surjectivity
reduces to an identity indexed by exactly `(⟨γ,δ⟩, 2s, 2s')` (§4).  The prior
large-bracket evidence (`s_exchange_identity*.py`, `s_ray_stress_multicover.py`)
reaches brackets `−6 … 10` in the **rank-2 pairwise** setting; this run does the
full random-word test at Kronecker-`k` for `k = 0…8`, 3-cycles up to `(6,6,6)`,
and random rank-3/4/5 lattices with entries to `±8`.  These are *not* dictionary
entries and are not claimed to be BPS quivers of anything; Conjecture 1 as stated
is about a lattice with an antisymmetric pairing, so they are legitimate test
objects, and they are reported separately so the two evidence classes are not
conflated.

#### Non-vacuity, measured rather than assumed

A sweep that never leaves cone degree 1, never produces spin and never produces a
negative multiplicity would pass trivially.  None of that holds here:

* **Content reaches the full cone depth** in every run (depth 6 at rank 2–3 in the
  dictionary run, 9 in the deep run).
* **The measured `Ω` carry far more spin than the inputs.**  Words seeded with
  `2s ≤ 4` re-factorize, in adversarial orders, into content reaching `2s = 31`
  on dictionary lattices and **`2s = 91`** (spin 45.5) at large brackets — every
  one of those multiplicities integral.  The existing exchange-identity evidence
  reaches `2s = 6`.
* **`Ω` is genuinely an integer, not a natural number**: 791 221 strictly
  negative multiplicities across the four runs.
* **The hard half is reached.**  331 543 measured multiplicities sit on charges
  with `gcd > 1` — §19 places the whole difficulty exactly there.
* **The order axis is live**: the factor count moves between orders on thousands
  of words.

#### A regularity, reported as an observation and not a claim

Across Kronecker-`k`, `k = 0…8`, the maximum spin the re-factorization is forced
to emit grows monotonically with the bracket: `2s = 5, 29, 39, 45, 52, 59, 63,
85, 86`.  The same trend appears on the 3-cycles (`(1,1,1) → 31`, `(6,6,6) → 76`)
and on the random lattices (cap 6 → 87).  This is a measurement of *this
harness's word distribution*, not a theorem about `𝓔`.  What it does say is that
the spin direction — the one the order search suppresses heuristically, and the
one `P_{21}` lives in — is exercised hardest exactly where the bracket is largest.

#### What this licenses, and what it does not

It does **not** prove surjectivity, and it does not touch the two sharp open
items: the `n ≥ 2` multi-cover cancellation in
`log A_γ(Ω) = Σ_n (−1)^n/(n[n]_𝖖) Ω^{(n)}(𝖖^n) Y_{nγ}`, and `P_{21}` in the
Chevalley-type presentation (§19 — *possibly not polynomial in `Ω`*).  Every run
is cone-truncated, which is intrinsic to any finite test of a pro-nilpotent
group; the depths reached are stated per run above.

What it does license, stated narrowly: over 43 248 factorizations on 1 177
lattices, spanning ranks 1–8, brackets `−8 … 8`, orders no central charge can
produce, and content to spin 45.5 — with the negative controls verified to bite —
Conjecture 1 has no counterexample in a region that includes, for the first time
for general elements of `𝓔`, **ranks 6–8** and **large brackets**.

### 6c. The rest of the Seiberg-Witten RG flow section (2026-09-04)

Continuing §6b with the other conjectures of that section, on the same
independent arithmetic (`experiments/pbw_e_group.py`; no shared code path with
`bps_factor_spectrum`, `recursive_spectrum` or `habiro`).  `S_DT = S` and
`S_CoHA = S` need geometric / CoHA input and are not touched.

#### Uniqueness of `S`, and `S_cluster = S`

`experiments/sw_flow_conjectures.py`, over the whole dictionary `n_001 … n_008`:

| claim | result |
|---|---|
| **uniqueness of `S`** — the same ELEMENT out of every order | **1108/1108** lattices |
| **`S_cluster` satisfies the BPS quiver constraint** | **2381/2381** specs |
| **`S_cluster == S`** | **2381/2381** specs |

Uniqueness is approached through order-independence: `S` is built by the forced
recursion in five total orders — degree-lex, **anti-degree** (every top-degree
factor before any node factor), lex-reversed, spin-first, and a shuffled order
of the truncated `Γ₊ × ½ℕ` — and the resulting elements are compared.  The
recursion itself is not independent evidence (it imposes the leading data by
construction); that the same element falls out of every order is the
measurement, and it is what uniqueness needs.

`S_cluster` is the paper's `∏_a E_𝖖(X_{γ(a)})` over a spec, ordered by
increasing `a`.  The paper flags the non-obvious half itself — *"Although
clearly `S_cluster ∈ 𝓔`, it is far from obvious that it satisfies
(eq:quiver)"* — and that is the first row: nothing about an ordered product of
plain `E_𝖖` factors forces its `𝖖`-expansion to have empty non-positive part
and `𝖖¹`-coefficient exactly `−1` on the nodes and `0` off them.  **Every known
chamber is tested, not one per quiver** (the conjecture quantifies over maximal
green sequences), which is why the spec count exceeds the lattice count; and
**2342 of the 2381 specs contain a charge that is not a node**, which is where
the claim has content.

**Controls (15/15).**  The `𝖖`-expansion of a coefficient two ways; `forced_omega`
verified to ACHIEVE the constraint it was derived for rather than assumed to
(40/40); `build_S_forced == bps_factor_spectrum` at pentagon / Kronecker-2 /
3-cycle(1,1,1) in the same `piece_key` order.  Negative: five wrong specs — the
reversed order, a node repeated, **a node missing**, a spurious extra charge,
the 3-state chamber reversed — must all violate the constraint, and do.

Two control failures on the way, both worth keeping:

* **The pentagon's `S` is the two node factors only in the order that puts `γ₁`
  first**; in degree-lex the same element needs 7 sign-alternating factors.
  That is order-dependence of the factorisation, not a defect — the same thing
  §6b's C7b/C7c pins.
* **A missing node was invisible.**  `leading_data_violations` iterated the
  SUPPORT of the element, so `spec = [γ₁]` on the pentagon — whose coefficient
  at `γ₂` is identically zero — reported zero violations and passed.  It now
  sweeps the whole truncated cone.  Worth recording because it is the
  cluster-side failure mode that matters: a spec with a node dropped is exactly
  what such a test must catch.

Also worth recording as a *positive*: `[γ₂, γ₁+γ₂, γ₁]` passes too.  It was
drafted as a negative control ("a non-node charge in the spec") and is nothing
of the kind — it is the pentagon identity, the genuine 3-state chamber.

#### The upper-cluster conjecture

`experiments/sw_upper_cluster.py`.  `RG_γ` is solved here from
`RG_γ·S = X_γ + O(𝖖)` directly: at each `κ` the equation reads
`acc + c_κ = O(𝖖)`, whose unique bar-invariant Laurent solution is
`−acc[0] − Σ_{n<0} acc[n](𝖖^n + 𝖖^{−n})`.

> **The `RG_γ` are Laurent polynomials — finite sums** (user ruling,
> 2026-09-04: *"no, F's should be Laurent polynomials"*).

That ruling retired a measurement this harness first attempted and should not
have.  An earlier version tried to *measure* termination, by asking whether the
`κ`-support stops strictly inside the truncated cone, and reported a large
"undetermined" bucket at rank ≥ 6.  Wrong twice over: termination is not in
doubt, and it is out of reach here anyway.  Read off `BPSKAlgebra.F` on
dictionary quivers, the top charge degree of `F` runs to 3 at rank 2, 10 at
rank 4, 14 at rank 5, 20 at rank 7 and **78** at the deepest seen — against a
feasible budget of 4–6, since the enumeration is `C(D+r, r)`.  So "the support
reached the budget" says nothing about termination; it says the budget was
small.  The bucket is removed.

What is measured instead, over 564 dictionary lattices (ranks 1–5 complete;
ranks 6–8 sampled at 80/60/26 of 484/200/26 — the sample sizes are printed, not
silent):

| claim | result |
|---|---|
| `RG_γ == BPSKAlgebra.F`, on every charge inside the window | **2982/2982** |
| **products CLOSE over `Z[𝖖, 𝖖⁻¹]`** — *"define a sub-algebra"* | **9714/9714** |

The first is independent cross-validation: an independent solver on an
independent `S`.  (Charges *above* the window are not comparable, and comparing
them was what made an earlier run look like a disagreement at rank ≥ 4 — the
differing charges were all of degree 8 against a window of 6.)

The second is the conjecture's own content.  `RG_γ·RG_δ` is decomposed in the
`RG` basis — forced and unique, since `RG_ε = X_ε + (strictly higher)` — and
every extracted coefficient is required to be an honest Laurent polynomial with
no surviving `(1−𝖖^{2n})` denominator.  Nothing in the construction forces
that.  Negative control: a `𝖖/(1−𝖖²)` perturbation of the product is *not*
absorbed, so the test bites.

The identification with the upper cluster algebra itself is **not** tested here;
that needs the cluster-side object and is a separate question from closure.

#### One measurement left open

At **Markov** the node-charge `RG` support tops at `κ`-degree 4 and stays there
for budgets 5, 6 and 7.  `kalgebra.md` ("S-finding") states the opposite for
that quiver — `upper(F_{γ_a})` landing exactly on the cone boundary at every
cutoff 6…10, *"so this is not a matter of raising the cutoff, and the natural
reading is that `F_{γ_a}`'s cone support is genuinely unbounded"*.  The `S` used
here is checked identical to `bps_factor_spectrum`'s at `D = 4, 5, 6`, so it is
not an `S` defect on this side, and `BPSKAlgebra` cannot be built at Markov (no
negating mutation sequence) so the usual cross-check is unavailable.  The two
statements are plausibly about different quantities — `upper()` is the upper
tropical label, a CHARGE, and its landing on a truncation boundary is a
statement about σ/ρ closing rather than about the cone DEGREE of the support
being bounded.  Flagged, not resolved.

### 6d. Factored RG flows (2026-09-04)

The last conjecture of that section reachable by computation
(`S_DT = S` and `S_CoHA = S` need geometric / CoHA input).  For a BPS quiver
`Q` and a FULL sub-quiver `Q'`, embedded in `Γ`: *"by picking an appropriate
total order, we can factor `S_Q = R_Q^{Q'} S_{Q'}`"*, and then `R_Q^{Q'}` is in
the image of `RG^{Q',Γ}`, with `RG^{Q,Γ}` factoring as
`RG^{Q',Γ} ∘ RG^{Q,Q',Γ}`.

Both halves reduce to one operation — decomposing an element in the `RG^{Q'}`
basis — because `RG^{Q'}_ε = X_ε + (strictly higher)` makes that decomposition
forced and unique.  So what is measured is never whether it *exists*
(triangularity gives that for anything supported on the cone) but **which ring
the coefficients land in**.

`experiments/sw_factored_flows.py`, over 1216 `(Q, Q')` pairs drawn from the
dictionary (ranks 2–8; entries sampled at 40 per file above rank 3, sub-quivers
at 6 per entry — the sample sizes are printed, not silent):

| claim | result |
|---|---|
| `S_Q = R · S_{Q'}` in the sub-last order | **1216/1216** |
| **`RG^{Q,Γ}` factors through `RG^{Q',Γ}` over `Z[𝖖,𝖖⁻¹]`** | **6824/6824** |

`S_{Q'}` is built on the sub-lattice and embedded, so it is the sub-quiver's own
spectrum generator rather than a re-solve inside `Γ`; the first row then checks
that `S_Q · S_{Q'}^{-1}` is exactly the ordered product of the factors at
charges *not* supported inside `Q'`, which is what "an appropriate total order"
asserts and which can fail.  The second row is the sharp half: `RG^{Q,Q',Γ}` is
an algebra map of `K_𝖖`-algebras, so its structure constants must be Laurent,
and nothing in the construction forces that.

**Controls (8/8).**  The two degenerate ends (`Q' = Q` gives `R = 1`;
`Q' = ∅` gives `R = S_Q`); the pentagon with one node dropped, by hand.
Negative: a perturbed `S_{Q'}` must break the factorisation, and does; and
decomposing against the **wrong** sub-quiver's `RG` basis must leave
non-Laurent coefficients, and does — without which the Laurent test would be
measuring nothing.

#### Where `S_Q^{Q'}` lives — a measurement, not a theorem

The paper closes the subsection by asking: *"It would be interesting to
characterize which pronilpotent group of formal sums in `K_𝖖(Q',Γ)` is the
natural place for such `S_Q^{Q'}` RG flow generating elements."*

Measured, on all 1216 pairs: of the **70 186** coefficients of `S_Q^{Q'}`,
exactly **1216** are honest Laurent polynomials — one per pair — and inspection
identifies it in every case as the **identity term**, the coefficient `1` at
charge `0`.  Every other coefficient genuinely carries a `(1−𝖖^{2n})`
denominator.

So `S_Q^{Q'} = 1 + (everything else, with denominators)`: the same shape as an
element of `ℰ` itself, but written on `K_𝖖(Q',Γ)`'s canonical basis instead of
on the `X_γ`.  Offered as a measurement of what the coefficients do on this
sample, not as a characterisation — the sample is dictionary quivers at cone
degree 4–6, and "is not Laurent here" is not "cannot be Laurent".

### 6e. Where `S_Q^{Q'}` lives — patterns (2026-09-04)

§6d closed the factored-flow conjecture and left one measurement: of the 70 186
coefficients of `S_Q^{Q'}` across 1216 pairs, exactly 1216 are Laurent — one per
pair, always the identity term.  This section chases the structure behind that,
answering the paper's closing question for the subsection: *"which pronilpotent
group of formal sums in `K_𝖖(Q',Γ)` is the natural place for such `S_Q^{Q'}`"*.

> **Stay in `𝓔`** (user ruling, 2026-09-04: *"I do not allow `E_{𝖖^n}`"*,
> *"stay in `𝓔`"*).  Recorded because an earlier version of this work violated
> it: on finding that the `E^{(s)}_𝖖(L_a)` subgroup does not contain every
> `S_Q^{Q'}`, it **enlarged the generator set** with `E_{𝖖^n}` — which is
> exactly the group the paper's own remark places outside `𝓔` (*"it does not
> include `E_{𝖖²}(x)`"*).  Enlarging the object is not finding the pattern.
> The ruling is right and the enlargement is retired.

#### One theorem, which narrows the target but does not settle it

`S_Q^{Q'}` is **bar-unitary**.  With `R := R_Q^{Q'} = S_Q S_{Q'}^{-1}`, and bar
antimultiplicative on the quantum torus,

    bar(R) = bar(S_{Q'})^{-1}·bar(S_Q) = S_{Q'}·S_Q^{-1} = R^{-1},

using `bar(S) = S^{-1}` for both spectrum generators; `RG` intertwines bar (it
sends the canonical basis to bar-invariant `F`s and acts on coefficients), so
`bar(S_Q^{Q'}) = (S_Q^{Q'})^{-1}` in `K_𝖖(Q',Γ)`.  Run as a control rather than
trusted.  It does not answer the question, because the bar-unitary group is
strictly larger than `𝓔` — the paper's own remark.

#### The home, and a proper subgroup of it

Two candidates, and the measurement separates them.  Over **580 `(Q,Q')` pairs**
(ranks 2–7, entries sampled at 20 per file above rank 3, sub-quivers at 6 per
entry — sizes printed, not silent):

| | |
|---|---|
| `R` lies in **`𝓔`** on the `X_γ`, exactly as the paper defines it | **580/580** |
| `R` lies in the subgroup generated by `E^{(s)}_𝖖(L_a)^{±1}` | **547/580** |

So the natural home is the **`RG^{Q',Γ}`-preimage of `𝓔`**, and the naive
transplant of `𝓔` onto the canonical basis is a **proper** subgroup of it —
strictly proper on 33 of 580 pairs.

The 33 are not an artifact.  They fail at the same charge under **seven**
different total orders (degree-lex, anti-degree, lex-reversed, spin-first and
three shuffles), and they survive a raised cutoff; on a separate sample the
split was 24/456 with `R ∈ 𝓔` on the torus for **all 24**.  Nor is it
degeneracy: degenerate (flavoured) pairings gave 226 ok / 8 fail against 92 ok /
10 fail for non-degenerate ones, so the flavoured quivers fail *less* often
proportionally.  (An earlier reading that the failures were all flavoured came
from a truncated printout — the harness prints only its first 15 failures.)

On every failing pair the residual that the `L`-basis read-off cannot absorb is
the same object: `−𝖖²/(1−𝖖⁴)` at spin 0 with multiplicity 1 — i.e. `−L_2` in the
note's notation `L_n = 𝖖^n/(1−𝖖^{2n})`, the family §"where a proof must bite"
singles out for `L_n/L_1 = 1/[n]_𝖖` being polynomial only at `n = 1`.  Recorded
as the shape of the obstruction; **not** as a licence to adjoin the
corresponding generator.

#### The leading data — the BPS quiver constraint, one algebra up

    S_Q^{Q'} = 1 − 𝖖 · Σ_{i ∉ Q'} L_{γ_i} + O(𝖖²)          580/580

Exactly `(eq:quiver)` with `X_γ → L_γ` and the sum over the **dropped** nodes:
every `𝖖¹` coefficient is `−1` (1510/1510), and the labels carrying them are
precisely the node charges of `Q` outside `Q'`.  And where the `E^{(s)}(L_a)`
subgroup does contain `S_Q^{Q'}`, that leading data **determines** it — the
forced recursion run over the `L`-generators rebuilds it exactly, **547/547**,
with the wrong leading data (all nodes rather than the dropped ones) rejected
**580/580**.

That forced recursion must read the coefficients in the **canonical basis**, not
the `X_γ` coefficients: they agree only at the lowest degree carrying content,
since lower `L`s contribute to higher `X`s.  Measured cost of getting it wrong —
the naive version rebuilds `S_Q^{Q'}` on 4/52 pairs, the correct one on 52/52.

#### Two more regularities

* **The support avoids `Q'` entirely**: 27 776 labels outside, **0** inside.
* **The denominators run**: `(1−𝖖^{2n})` occurs for `n = 1…6` with counts
  27 776 / 21 899 / 10 379 / 3 627 / 949 / 148 — no bound at `n = 1`.  Exactly
  one coefficient per pair is Laurent (580/28 356), always the identity term,
  reproducing §6d's count on this sample.

#### What is open

Whether the `RG^{Q',Γ}`-preimage of `𝓔` has a *generators-and-relations*
description intrinsic to `K_𝖖(Q',Γ)` — the paper's question in its sharpest
form — is not settled here.  What is settled is that the obvious candidate is
too small, and by how much: 33 of 580, with the deficit always of the shape
`−L_2` at spin 0.

## 7. Crystalline DT = DT = the true spec (user conjecture + direction ruling, 2026-08-13)

> **Conjecture (user, verbatim).** *"I am conjecturing of course that crystal DT is
> the same as DT is the same as the true spec."*

and the accompanying ruling on where the repo is going:

> **Direction (user, verbatim).** *"As we have a spec finder and now a crystalline
> S-finder, one can test this by comparing the two if needed. But I am happy to
> assume the conjecture they are the same. It is the general spirit of the repo.
> Use crystalline definitions to replace cluster notions."*

**Vocabulary.** "Crystal" / "crystalline" here is the user's own, and it is the
title of `pronilpotent_group_note.tex` — *"A crystal definition of the
Donaldson–Thomas element for BPS quivers"*.  So the **crystalline `S`-finder** is
the construction of this note as implemented in `bps_factor_spectrum.py`: leading data
plus palindromic BPS factors, no spec and no green sequence.  The **spec finder**
is the cluster-side route (`bps_quiver_tools`' green-sequence / mutation search,
`recursive_spectrum.extract_spec_from_quiver`).  The **true spec** is a spec in the
strict sense — carrying the green/red node condition.

**What the ruling changes in practice.**  Where a construction currently needs a
*cluster* notion (a chamber, a green sequence, a mutation path) and a crystalline
one is available, prefer the crystalline one, and do not add cluster structure to
justify it.  Two consequences already realised in the code:

* A **finite factorization with `s = 0` only** is what consumers actually need —
  not a true spec (user, 2026-08-13: *"even spec extraction does not need chamber
  physics.  A true spec requires a condition on green/red nodes, but we do not
  necessarily need a true spec.  Any finite factorization with s=0 only would do
  the job for us"*).  `extract_spec_from_quiver` already delivers exactly that: it
  returns charges with `S = ∏ E_𝖖(X_{spec_i})` and **verifies the rebuild over the
  full cone**, so it is spin-0-only and finite by construction, whatever order
  built its input `S`.
* Hence **no central charge is needed anywhere on that path**, which is what
  licensed making the engine's default order central-charge-free (§8 below).

**Existing evidence, and how far it goes.**  The element-level half is measured
broadly: over the canonical BPS-quiver dictionary, **1108/1108** entries at ranks
1–8 give crystalline `S` `==` `Theory.S_from_spec(spec)` `==` the peel engine's `S`
(`experiments/s_ray_spectrum_dictionary_sweep.py`), and the finite-type battery
recovers hypermultiplets at positive roots with zero off-root content (§6).

*An observation offered for the user to judge, not a proof.*  The element-level
agreement plus **proved injectivity of `μ_σ`** (§4) already gives the content-level
statement *in a fixed order*: if the crystalline `S` equals `S_from_spec(spec)`,
and the factorisation of a given element in a given order is unique, then in the
order matching the spec's own the crystalline content **must be** that spec.  So
what remains genuinely open in "crystal DT = true spec" is not the identification
itself but whether the spec's order is one the builder realises — which is exactly
what the order relaxations of §8 widen.  Worth checking before leaning on.

---

## 8. Order search: greedy is not expected to work; a BFS over orderings is (recorded, 2026-08-13)

> **User, verbatim.** *"I think we will not find easy greedy heuristics when building
> S step by step.  A \*good\* move would be recognized by the fact that subsequent
> moves are easier.  But we could have BFS search method which explores different
> factor ordering and selects for simpler factorizations (smaller s, smaller Ω,
> etc.) in the hope of landing a spec (finite product of `E_𝖖` factors)."*

**IMPLEMENTED (2026-08-13): `factor_order_search.py`**, battery
`tests/test_factor_order_search.py`, benchmark
`experiments/s_factor_order_search_benchmark.py`.  What is searched: placements of the
individual `(s, γ)` pieces (§7's finer relaxation, now the engine's own contract —
`BPSFactorSpectrum(piece_key=…)`), with a preference for factorisations that stay simple —
bounded spin, small `|Ω|`, ideally spin-0 only, which is the "finite product of
`E_𝖖` factors" the search is hoping to land.

**The layers are cone degrees, and the cost is an overall count** (user: *"with
looking ahead I did not just mean to the next move.  more like an overall 'cost'
given by the number of terms with a dislike for `s>0` as well"*):

    cost  =  terms  +  SPIN_PENALTY·Σ|a_s|·2s ,   over everything placed
             PLUS the same weighted count of what is already FORCED at the next degree.

The forced terms are counted rather than used as a tiebreak because `_readout` fixes
them from what is placed and nothing later can change them — they are as much a
property of the candidate as its own factors.  Keeping them in the count is also what
lets the cost separate *siblings*: within one degree the forced `Ω` is already
determined before any of that degree's factors is placed, so children of one parent
share it and a count of placed terms alone is constant across exactly the set it is
asked to rank.

**Why suppress spin at all** (user): an `s > 0` factor implies — believed, not proved
— infinitely many more factors, hence content that never stops populating, hence not
a spec.  So the spin preference is the observable proxy for termination, not an
aesthetic.

**And sparsity is the goal in its own right** (user: *"a sparsely populated `S` helps
with calculations too"*).  Measured, the signal is stark and *grows* with the cutoff:
a good order's support is constant in `D` while a bad one's tracks the cone
(Kronecker-3 at `D = 6 → 12`: 2 charges throughout, against 17 → 68 of 27 → 90 cone
points, 63 % → 76 % of the cone).  That is why the search separates good from bad
easily — and why, on a quiver with **no** spec, it drops the spin-0 prune and returns
the sparsest order rather than nothing: Markov 16 rays / `2s ≤ 5` → 7 / 1,
3-cycle(3,3,3) 17 / 9 → 10 / 5, 4-cycle(2) 25 / 5 → 11 / 2.

**What is exact and what is not**, kept separate because a search reports negatives:

* **Exact** — a branch dies the moment a forced `Ω` carries a nonzero spin
  (`require_spin_zero`) or a negative multiplicity (`require_positive`).  `Ω` is
  forced, so a violating branch can never recover; this is a decision, not a
  heuristic, and it is what makes the search selective rather than an enumeration.
* **Heuristic** — `keep_per_degree`, how many candidate orders are carried forward
  from each cone degree.  `Result.exhaustive` reports whether that cap or the branch
  cap bit, so a negative answer is a proof only when it says so.  It genuinely bites:
  at `keep_per_degree = 2` the SU(3)-cyclic 6-factor spec is lost outright *and* the
  5-cycle returns a 9-factor answer where the default finds 8 — and that 9-factor
  answer is not merely worse, it is **wrong** one degree past the cutoff (see the
  stress campaign below).

  **But a single run is a DRAW, and the seed decides what it finds** (measured
  2026-08-14).  `_positions` samples once the position count exceeds its cap, so
  the width is not the whole story — and at one fixed width the draws span every
  possible outcome.  cycle6 at `D = 7`, at the **default** width, varying only the
  seed: seeds 1 and 3 give a certified 10-factor spec, seeds 2 and 4 give nothing,
  seed 5 gives a 10-factor content exact to degree 7 and wrong at 8.  Likewise at
  the default width on two rank-5 dictionary entries, seeds 1–8 give
  `- - - - - - 8 8` and `- - 9 - - 9 9 9`.

  ⚠ **This corrects a first reading of the same data.**  Widening was tried first
  and appeared to be the mechanism — "width 2 beats width 4 at cycle6", "width 16
  finds what width 4 cannot".  Both were sampling artifacts: width 4 also wins at
  cycle6, at other seeds, and both dictionary answers are reachable at the width
  that first reported nothing.  The discrepancy surfaced only because two runs of
  the same quantity disagreed — a fixed-width sweep against an escalation that had
  inherited an already-advanced random state.  No width claim in this module
  should be read without
  a seed attached.

  So the response is to **restart on failure** (`_escalate`: `RESTARTS` fresh
  draws at the same width, then widening as a last resort, and only when the pass
  returned no spec at all).  Restarts are the right dial for a reason worth
  stating: widths are not ordered by quality, so no width is "the right one" —
  the shape of error that produced `STOP_MARGIN` twice — whereas restarts are
  **monotone**, since more draws can only find more.  Escalation is guarded by the
  same certificate, inert on success, and recovers **both** rank-5 dictionary
  entries that previously found no spin-0 order, at 8 and 9 factors.

**Results, all in-cone.**  Nothing here establishes that a factorisation
terminates — the recursion is solved to a finite cutoff `D` and *"the S-builder will
never be 'done' typically"* (user).  What is reported is that `S` restricted to the
cone equals the ordered `E_𝖖` product (verified by rebuilding through
`Theory.S_from_spec`), that factors **stopped appearing strictly below `D`** —
the user's own characterisation of a spec, *"a 'spec' `S` will just stop
populating at some point"* — and that the product still reproduces `S` on a
**strictly wider cone** than the one that produced it.  The third clause is not
decoration: without it the first two admit impostors (see the stress campaign
below).  Measured: every spec found stops at degree 1–4 against cutoffs 4–6.

On an acyclic quiver the search does not run at all — the source/sink
strip already attains the **provable floor** (at cone degree 1 the accumulated
product is empty, so `Ω` is forced nonzero at every node in every order; hence no
factorisation has fewer than `rank` factors, and the strip has exactly `rank`).
Where the strip leaves a core, which is precisely where the engine's default falls
back to random placement, the search collapses **13–29 rays carrying spin up to
`2s = 9` into 4–6 spin-0 factors**: 3-cycle(1,1,1) 13 → 4, 3-cycle(2,1,1) 19 → 4,
3-cycle(2,2,1) 29 → 4, SU(3)-cyclic 18 → 6.  Markov and 3-cycle(3,3,3) correctly
report no spin-0 order, with `exhaustive=True`.

**On two quivers it is the crystalline route that DELIVERS**, which is worth saying
because `extract_spec_from_quiver` is otherwise the cheaper tool and the natural
default.  That extractor exceeds a 60 s box on **A6 linear** and on **5-cycle(1)** —
the unbounded 5-cycle run reached 2.7 GB RSS before being killed — where the order
search answers in 0.10 s (via the acyclic short-circuit) and 4.84 s, and the
cluster-side BFS in ~0.02 s.  So the three routes are complementary in cost as well
as in mechanism, and none of them dominates.

**This is a data point for §7's conjecture** (crystal DT = DT = the true spec), and a
non-trivial one: on every quiver where a spin-0 factorisation exists in-cone, the order
search, the crystalline extractor `extract_spec_from_quiver` and the **cluster-side**
`BPSQuiver.find_negating_sequence` agree on its **existence and its length**.  They
do *not* always agree on the charges — at the 3-cycles the three routes return three
different valid 4-factor specs — which is expected, since specs are not unique and
`S` is; at SU(3)-cyclic all three coincide as sets.  Every reported factorisation
is rebuilt by a Nahm-sum expansion sharing no code with the ray recursion before
it is reported — `Theory.S_from_spec` for a spin-0 spec, and since 2026-08-14
`nahm_local.general_nahm_habiro` for a content carrying spin.

**The spin-only limit was never mathematical** (user, 2026-08-14: *"you certainly
know the series for E and E^{-1} ... they are related by `𝖖 ↔ 𝖖⁻¹` anyway"*).
`_nahm_shift` carried an implicit all-ones LINEAR term and the off-diagonal
`k_{ab}` and no DIAGONAL — exactly the shape of a product of plain
`E_𝖖(X_{γ_a})`.  Since `E_𝖖(x)^{-1} = Σ_n 𝖖^{n²}x^n/(𝖖²;𝖖²)_n` is `E_𝖖` at
`𝖖 → 𝖖⁻¹`, inversion is what supplies the `n²`, and a `𝖖^j`-scaled argument only
moves the linear coefficient.  Restoring both reaches every BPS factor:
multiplicity was *already* reachable (a repeated charge), integer spin needs only
the linear coefficient, and half-integer spin needs the diagonal.  The consequence
that matters is that the order search's **sparse fallback** — which carries spin
and so had no independent check at all — is now verified, measured at
Markov(2,2,2) and at 3-cycle(3,3,3) with spin up to `2s = 5`.

### Terminology: *impostor* (approved by the user, 2026-08-14)

> **impostor** — a factorisation whose ordered `E_𝖖` product agrees with `S` at
> every cone degree it was verified at, and disagrees at some higher degree.

Not merely *wrong* (it is exact everywhere it was checked) and not merely
*suboptimal* (the sharp 5-cycle pair share a top degree, and the impostor is the
*shorter* of the two).  The point of the word is precisely that no predicate
evaluated inside the verified cone separates it from the real answer.

**This is reuse, not coinage.**  The repo already uses *impostor* in exactly this
sense — `residue_cancellation_recognition.md` §"So (★) + bar alone do not pin the
canonical, and what kills the impostor is precisely `O(𝖖)`", and the same
sentence in `experiments/oq_bubbling_solver.py` — for a candidate that satisfies
every check applied to it and is still not the object wanted.  What is new here is
only the class of object it is applied to: factorisations rather than canonical
basis elements.

*Provenance:* the term was in use in this module's docstrings and audit entries
before it was proposed, which was the wrong order; raised 2026-08-14 and ruled by
the user the same day (*"If you think 'impostor' needs a name go ahead"*).  Kept
because it recurs across the module docstring, `repo_audit.md` A53/A56, three
design docs and two test names, and the alternative is a fifteen-word description
repeated at each site.

### The stress campaign (2026-08-13) — and what it broke

> **User.** *"continue testing, pushing cutoff in the cone, looking at higher rank,
> intricate quivers, etc."*

**A certificate that a single extra degree invalidates.**  The first thing pushing
the cutoff found was a defect in the acceptance criterion, not a limit of the
search.  At **4-cycle(1), `D = 4`** the search returns a 6-factor spin-0 content
topping out at degree 3 which rebuilds `S` on the cone up to 4 and is **wrong from
degree 5 on** — differing from the valid factorisation *only by the order of two
adjacent charges*.  The rebuild is in-cone by necessity, so it certifies exactly
what it saw.  Measured over 84 checks (find at `D`, re-verify at `D+1, D+2, D+3`):
every failure had margin `≤ 1`, every margin `≥ 2` passed, where margin =
`cutoff − top_degree`.  Hence `STOP_MARGIN = 2` (`repo_audit.md` A52).

**And then the margin itself was refuted — a margin cannot be the certificate at
all** (`repo_audit.md` A53).  The 84 checks covered seven quivers; the eighth broke
the rule.  **cycle6 at `D = 7`**: a 10-factor content with margin 2, exact on the
whole cone up to 7 and wrong at 8 — while cycle5 at margin 2 *is* valid two degrees
up, so no larger constant repairs it.  Sharper still, **the 5-cycle at `D = 6`**
holds a 9-factor impostor and the valid 8-factor answer at the **same top degree**:
same quiver, same cutoff, same margin, one exact only up to 6 and the other up to
8.  No margin of any size separates those two.

So the acceptance is now a real check rather than a calibrated proxy:
`CONFIRM_EXTRA = 1` rebuilds `S` and the candidate product at `degree_cap + 1` and
requires agreement there, with `STOP_MARGIN` demoted to the cheap screen that
decides whether to pay for it.  The corrected methodological rule — the one A52
got wrong — is: **when a check can only see inside a truncation, do not calibrate
how far inside; check outside.**  Blast radius measured and nil: the dictionary
sweep is unchanged at 16/16 and 74/74 with the same 50 shortenings, so the
certificate rejects no real answer.

**Where the margin is ample the answer is stable.**  On 3-cycle(1,1,1),
3-cycle(2,1,1) and SU(3)-cyclic the *identical* spec returns at every cutoff from
4 to 8, top degree and ray count constant, while the cone grows 34 → 164 points;
cost is near-linear in cone size.

**Higher rank, and the one structural prediction the search makes.**  Acyclic
quivers short-circuit and stay trivial to rank 8 (0.31 s).  For cycles there is a
law, read off ranks 3–6 and then **confirmed out of sample at ranks 7 and 8**:

    cycle_n  →  spec length 2(n−1),  top degree n−1

verified at ranks 3–8, exactly.  Timings after the optimization below: 0.11 s,
0.74 s, 3.16 s, 11.4 s, 137.9 s at ranks 4–8.

The law originally carried a third clause — *"so cutoff `≥ n+1`, and `n+1` is the
smallest that certifies"* — and **that clause is where the cycle6 counterexample
lives**: at `D = 7` cycle6 produces exactly the predicted shape (10 factors, top
degree 5) and is wrong at degree 8.  Re-measured under the wider-cone certificate,
the smallest certifying cutoff is **not monotone in the rank at all**:

| rank | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 7 | 8 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| smallest certifying cutoff | `n+1` | `n+1` | `n+1` | **`n+2`** | **`n+2`** | `n+1` |

(cycle7: refused at `D = 8`, granted at `D = 9`; cycle8: granted at `D = 9`, i.e.
`n+1`, 524 s.)  Ranks 6 and 7 need the extra degree and rank 8 does not, so no
constant offset — and no margin — was ever going to be the rule.  The structural
half of the law is untouched at every rank measured; only its cutoff prediction
was an artifact of certifying on the margin.

**Intricate quivers — the canonical dictionary at cutoff 5.**  Rank 3: 16/16
entries yield a spec.  Rank 4: 74/74.  Zero rebuild failures against
`Theory.S_from_spec` over the full cone.  And the result worth the campaign:

> **On rank 4, 50 of 74 factorisations are strictly SHORTER than the catalogued
> spec** — 24 equal, **zero longer** — with every shortened case landing on `rank`
> factors, the provable floor.

Split by route, because they are two different statements: the **BFS** produced 27
of them (against 11 equal) on cored quivers, and the **acyclic strip
short-circuit** the other 23 (against 13 equal).  So the mantle order beats the
catalogued spec about as often as the search does, and neither ever returns a
longer one.

Controlled with the lesson above: a shorter spec found at cutoff 5 was re-verified
at cutoff **7** alongside the dictionary's own, and both rebuild there on all six
sampled entries.  These are genuinely smaller chambers of the same `S`; the
dictionary's specs are simply not minimal.  Harness:
`experiments/s_factor_order_search_dictionary.py`.

**Rank 5 completes the picture**: 305 entries, 297 factorisations, **263 strictly
shorter** than the catalogued spec, 34 equal, zero longer; sparser than the
default order on 229, mean factor **4.00×**.  Only 2 entries genuinely found
nothing — six more were candidates refused on margin.  Across ranks 3–5 that is
387 factorisations found and 320 of them shorter than the dictionary's.

**And the whole campaign was RE-MEASURED under the wider-cone certificate**
(2026-08-14), because every number above was an acceptance made under the
`STOP_MARGIN` rule that was later refuted, and an impostor is by construction the
thing an in-cone check cannot see.  All three ranks come back **bit-for-bit
identical** — 16/16, 74/74 and 297/305, the same 263 shortenings at rank 5 with
the same 4.00× mean sparsity — so **the certificate rejected none of the 387**,
and the headline survives unchanged.

⚠ **Read that as "verified to `cutoff + 1`", not as "correct".**  The
re-measurement ran at `CONFIRM_EXTRA = 1`, and depth 1 was itself refuted the
same day (`repo_audit.md` A56: cycle6 at `D = 7`, seed 1, passes at depth 1 and
is wrong at 9).  So the 387 are checked one degree past their cutoff and no
further; each carries its own `Result.confirmed_to`, and nothing above it is
claimed.  Saying "none was an impostor" would be exactly the over-claim this
whole sequence of refutations is about.

Re-run at **depth 2**, every acceptance across all three ranks **holds** — 16,
74 and 298, so **388 with none falling** one degree further out.  Stated with the
same discipline: that establishes those 388 are verified to `cutoff + 2`, and it
is *not* evidence that depth 2 suffices, which is the inference refuted three
times already.  The cheap thing it does buy is a bound on how common the failure
is: the two known cases are cycle6 and the 5-cycle, and nothing in the catalogued
quivers behaves that way at these cutoffs.

Two details in that count rather than smoothed over.  Rank 5 reads **298**, not
the 297 recorded above, because the restart escalation now rescues an entry that
previously found nothing; and it is 298 rather than 299 because the ladder draws
a fixed set of seeds, so the second rescued entry depends on which draws it
happens to make — the same sampling sensitivity as above, surfacing in the
totals.  Rank 5 now costs 160 s for its 305 entries.  Worth
saying where the impostors *do* live, since this is a null result about them:
both known ones sit at a cutoff high relative to the rank (cycle6 at `D = 7`, the
5-cycle at `D = 6` under a narrowed beam), not at the dictionary's cutoff 5 —
which is consistent with the mechanism, since a factorisation has to have
*stopped* well inside the cone before it can be exact there and wrong above.

**Cost.**  Profiling put 95 % of the runtime in one place — rebuilding the
accumulated product — and the fix was to notice that *ranking* needs only the
terms forced at the next cone degree, which is a readout on a much smaller cone.
Scoring candidates on a cone truncated to `d+1` and building the full product
only for survivors gives **10.6×** at cycle6 (33.0 s → 3.12 s) and **29.5×** at
cycle7 (336 s → 11.4 s) — the gain grows with the cone, as it should.  Two
smaller changes are recorded with it, one worth 1.37× and one measured *neutral*
and kept anyway.

**Machinery it was built on**, for the record:

* `experiments/s_free_order_uniqueness.py` already branched over arbitrary
  placements with **exact positivity pruning**, and reported the branch counts:
  pentagon 2, Kronecker-2 43, 3-cycle(1,1,1) 9, Markov 187 (cap 200),
  Kronecker-3/-4 400 (cap-limited).  Those caps are exactly where the selective
  search earns its keep over enumeration.
* `BPSFactorSpectrum` supplies all the arithmetic — the cone, the readout, `_forced`, the
  ray multiply — so the search owns the *order* and nothing else, and any
  factorisation it reports is one the engine itself would produce given the same
  placement.
* Placements form a **trace monoid** (two BPS factors commute exactly when
  `⟨γ,δ⟩ = 0`), so equivalent orders are merged by a lexicographic normal form —
  integer work only, and sound in the safe direction (it never conflates two
  genuinely different states).

**Measured support for the pessimism about greedy.**  The one heuristic that *does*
hit the optimum is not greedy at all — it is a **global** combinatorial property of
the quiver (the source/sink strip / mantle theorem), and it reaches exactly `rank`
rays, spin-0 only, on every acyclic quiver measured.  Where it does not apply (the
strip leaves a core) no cheap local rule was found: the identity order it degenerates
to measures *worse than a random permutation* (15 rays against a best of 6; 70 against
13), and the best cheap substitute found was a **low-cutoff probe** — i.e. a small
lookahead, not a greedy step — which picked the full-cutoff winner in 4 of 6 cases
with regret 1.07–1.17× otherwise (`s_leading_term_existence.md` §26,
`experiments/s_ray_order_heuristics.py`).  That a *lookahead* works where a local rule
does not is the same shape as the user's remark: a good move is recognised by later
moves being easier.
