## 9. The joint `F_γ`/`S` builder (user direction, 2026-08-13; `fs_builder.py`)

> **User, verbatim.**  *"The crystalline S builder suggests a crystalline builder
> for `F_γ S` which does not rely on S but rather directly solves for
> `FS = X_γ + O(𝖖)` by adding at each steps either `E^{(s)}_𝖖(X_γ')` factors to S
> or (palindromic) `X_{γ+γ'}` summands to F."*

Built: `fs_builder.py` (`FSBuilder`, entry point `build_F_and_S`), battery
`tests/test_fs_builder.py`, bulk sweep `experiments/fs_builder_dictionary_sweep.py`.

**Name ruled by the user, 2026-08-13: `FSBuilder` / `fs_builder.py`.**  The
earlier `RayFS` / `ray_fs.py` was rejected the same day, and for a reason worth
keeping: *"ray" names the wrong unit* — the placement unit is the individual
`E^{(s)}_𝖖(X_{γ'})^{Ω(s,γ')}` piece, not the whole BPS factor at `γ'`.

### 9a. Why it works: the linear sector of an enlarged quiver (user, 2026-08-13)

> **User, verbatim.**  *"note that the summands can also be placed in various
> locations, I write it as "FS" but it could be a sum of terms with X's inserted at
> different locations between the E's. The logic is simple. Take the BPS quiver and
> add a new node `γ + γ_0` with pure flavour `γ_0`. The[n] I believe the new
> `S_{new}` then is `S_{new} = S − 𝖖/(1−𝖖²) X_{γ_0} F_γ S + O(X_{2 γ_0})`. That is
> why building for FS is like a partially linearized piece of building `S_new`."*

Adjoin one node at `γ + γ_0` with `γ_0` a **pure flavour** direction, so `X_{γ_0}`
is central and `Γ' = Γ ⊕ Z·γ_0` has the new row and column of the pairing zero.
Then the `X_{γ_0}`-degree-0 sector of `S_new` is the old `S`, and its **linear**
sector is `−𝖖/(1−𝖖²)·X_{γ_0}·F_γ S`.  Two things fall out at once:

* the joint `F`/`S` recursion of §9 **is** the crystalline `S` recursion on the
  enlarged quiver, linearised in `X_{γ_0}` — one construction, not two
  interleaved ones.  `𝖖/(1−𝖖²) = −c_1` is the BPS factor's own tail, i.e. the
  leading data `−1` at the new node, which is also why `F_γ`'s coefficient at `γ`
  comes out `1` rather than being imposed;
* **`F_γ·S` is a presentation, not the object.**  The linear sector is a sum of
  terms with the new `X` monomials inserted at *various positions* among the old
  `E_𝖖` factors — one position per BPS factor of the enlarged quiver — and
  collecting them on the far left is what turns that sum into a product.  The
  §3 order-independence of `S_new` is what makes the presentations agree.

**Measured** (`experiments/fs_builder_enlarged_quiver.py`; pentagon ×2, Kronecker-2,
Kronecker-3, 3-cycle, Markov; every charge of the old cone, so the converse is
tested and not only `F`'s own support):

| | leftmost | rightmost | interleaved |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| `X_{γ_0}`-degree-0 sector `==` old `S` | 124/124 | 124/124 | 124/124 |
| linear sector `==` `c_1·F_γ S` | 124/124 | 124/124 | 124/124 |
| `Ω` at `γ+γ_0+δ` `==` `F_γ`'s coefficient `c_δ` | **124/124** | 99/124 | 62/124 |

The identity is a statement about the **element** and survives every placement;
the multiplicities coincide with `F_γ`'s coefficients **only** in the leftmost
placement — which is exactly what "writing it as `FS`" picks out.  A battery that
ran only the leftmost order would be presenting a gauge choice as a fact, so the
discriminator is pinned in `tests/test_fs_builder.py`.

**Notation (user's, 2026-08-13): `ω(s,γ')` for the summand multiplicities.**
Beside the established `Ω(s,γ')` — the multiplicity of the spin-`s` piece of the
BPS factor at `γ'`, i.e. `Ω_{γ'} = Σ_s Ω(s,γ')·χ_s` — the user writes `ω(s,γ')`
for the `F`-side counterpart: the multiplicity of the spin-`s` piece of the
summand at `γ+γ'`, so that summand is `ω(s,γ')·χ_s·X_{γ+γ'}`.  Lower case for the
`F` side, upper case for the `S` side.

**`𝖖`-numbers: one definition, the repo's** (user ruling, 2026-08-13 —
*"`[2s]_𝖖` should have been `[2s+1]_𝖖`"*, and *"there should be only a natural
definition of `𝖖`-numbers, do not proliferate bracket"*).  That definition is
`q_number_poly.QNumberPoly`'s, which the `F`-solver already carries coefficients
in:

    [n]_𝖖  =  𝖖^{−(n−1)} + 𝖖^{−(n−3)} + ⋯ + 𝖖^{n−1}       (n terms; [1] = 1)

so the spin-`s` multiplet, of dimension `2s+1`, is

    χ_s  =  𝖖^{−2s} + ⋯ + 𝖖^{2s}  =  [2s+1]_𝖖 .

`χ_s` stays the `S`-side's working notation (it is what `Ω = Σ_s a_s χ_s` is
written in); `[n]_𝖖` means this and nothing else.

*One assistant reservation, recorded and not acted on:* §9a's measurement says
these are not two kinds of object — in the enlarged quiver a summand at `γ+γ'`
**is** a spin piece of the BPS factor at `γ+γ_0+γ'`, and at leftmost placement
`ω(s,γ')` is literally `Ω(s, γ+γ_0+γ')` — so two symbols may suggest a
distinction the construction does not make.  Against that, the two do sit in
different sectors and a reader needs to know which is meant.  The user's notation
stands.

**Arbitrary placement of the summands, not only of the `E`'s** (user, 2026-08-13:
*"we should allow arbitrary placements of the `ω(s,γ') [2s]_𝖖 X_{γ+γ'}`
summands!"*).  In the enlarged quiver a summand at `γ+γ'` **is** a spin piece of
the BPS factor at `γ+γ_0+γ'`, so one per-`(s, charge)` placement rule places both
kinds and no second mechanism is needed.  That rule is `BPSFactorSpectrum(piece_key=…)`
(mode `"pieces"`), which also settles what that module recorded as an open
question — `order_key` is a function of the charge and so cannot separate `γ`'s
spin pieces.  Consumer: `fs_builder.fs_linear_sector`.

Measured (`experiments/fs_builder_enlarged_quiver.py`), six placement rules
including ones that interleave the summands *between* the `E` factors rather than
collecting them at either end, over pentagon ×2 / Kronecker-2 / Kronecker-3 /
3-cycle / Markov:

> `F_γ S` is **invariant**: 480/480 in-window coefficients, every rule.

So the **object** is placement-independent — the `F`-side counterpart of the
`S`-side order-independence the construction rests on — while only its *split
into summands* is not.  ⚠ The comparison is in-window by necessity: the reference
`F·S` is formed from an `F` and an `S` each truncated at the cutoff, so beyond
that degree it is not a complete product, and counting those charges would
manufacture disagreements that are truncation rather than placement.

**The `γ_0`-tower beyond `n = 1` is NOT a tower — assistant extrapolation,
refuted.**  Having measured the `O(X_{2γ_0})` sector as `c_2·F_{2γ}·S` on five
quivers, the assistant suggested `S_new = Σ_n c_n X_{nγ_0} F_{nγ} S`.  The user's
reply: *"I do not expect `S_new = Σ_n c_n X_{nγ_0} F_{nγ} S` to be true"* — and
measurement agrees with the user.  It survives `n = 2, 3` on pentagon /
Kronecker-2 / 3-cycle(1,1,1), and **fails at Markov, `γ = (1,0,0)`**, at 4 of 20
charges for both `n = 2` and `n = 3`
(`experiments/fs_builder_enlarged_quiver.py::tower`).

The mechanism, which is what makes the negative useful: the tower needs the whole
`γ_0`-graded tower of `S_new` to be generated by the single BPS factor at
`γ + γ_0`, its `n`-th power supplying `c_n`.  At Markov `γ = (1,0,0)` the enlarged
quiver has factors of its own at `γ_0`-degree 2 — `(2,0,1,2)`, `(2,0,3,2)`,
`(2,1,2,2)`, `(2,1,3,2)` — that are powers of nothing at degree 1, and the
degree-1 sector already carries **spin** (`Ω = 𝖖^{-1}+𝖖`).  So the tower holds
exactly where the `γ_0`-tower is one factor's powers — the same condition as §9c's
single-insertion collapse, and Markov `γ = (1,0,0)` is precisely the charge that
failed to collapse there.  **One boundary, two symptoms.**  The `n = 1` identity
— the user's, above — is untouched by this and holds everywhere measured.

**A third, independent route to `F_γ` follows**, and is shipped as
`fs_builder.F_from_enlarged_quiver`: build `S_new` on the enlarged quiver with the
new factors leftmost and **read `F_γ` off `Ω`** — no `F` recursion anywhere in
it, only `BPSFactorSpectrum`.  Measured equal to both the joint recursion and
`BPSKAlgebra.F_qn`.  It costs more than §9's recursion (a rank-`r+1` cone one
degree deeper, and it builds the `O(X_{2γ_0})` sectors the linearisation never
forms), so it is the cross-check and `FSBuilder` stays the working route.

### 9c. Letting the order depend on `γ`: `F_γ` is a conjugate of a monomial

> **User, 2026-08-13, verbatim.**  *"I think letting the order of factors in S
> depend on the choice of `γ` may make the FS builder better than building S and
> finding F in the usual way…"* … *"so test and benchmark and optimize"*

It does, and structurally rather than by a constant.  The joint builder never
needs a *canonical* `S`: `S` is order-independent, so the order is free, and —
unlike build-`S`-once-then-solve — it may be chosen **per `γ`**.  Choose it by
running §8's order search on the **enlarged quiver** of §9a, which is itself a
function of `γ`.  What comes back, wherever that quiver is **acyclic**, is the
node-charge spec (`rank + 1` factors, spin 0, `optimal=True`), whose
`X_{γ_0}`-linear sector has **exactly one** surviving piece — the bare `X_γ` at
multiplicity `χ_0`:

    F_γ S  =  E_1 · X_γ · E_2 ,      S = E_1 · E_2 ,

`E_1`, `E_2` the old nodes' factors before and after the new node's position in
the strip order — **a position that depends on `γ`** (measured at the pentagon:
between the two old factors at `γ = (1,1)`, last at `γ = (−1,1)`).  Equivalently

    F_γ  =  E_1 · X_γ · E_1^{-1} ,

a conjugate of a bare monomial.  Nothing is solved, no `Ω` is forced at any
charge, and the doubly-tropical interval never appears.  Against it, the leftmost
presentation of the *same element* spreads `F_γ` over up to 10 charges on these
quivers.

**Measured** (`experiments/fs_builder_gamma_order.py`, `fs_builder.fs_closed_form`,
battery in `tests/test_fs_builder.py`):

| | |
|---|---:|
| charges where the `F` side collapses to ONE insertion | **13/14** |
| the element is right in the γ-dependent order | **190/190** |
| closed form `==` the joint recursion's `F·S`, in-window | **exact, every case** |
| closed form vs the joint recursion | **1.5–4.4×** faster, growing with the cutoff |
| closed form vs build-`S`-and-solve, Kronecker-3 | **3–16×** faster |

⚠ **Two limits, both measured rather than assumed.**  Against the shipped
`solve_F` the closed form wins at Kronecker-3 and *loses* at the pentagon and A3,
where that route is a tuned spec-mode path — so "better" is a statement about the
construction, not a uniform speed claim.  And **acyclicity is SUFFICIENT, NOT
NECESSARY**: an earlier reading of this measurement asserted "the collapse happens
exactly where the enlarged quiver is acyclic" and was **wrong** — the 3-cycle(1,1,1)
collapses to a single insertion with no strip and no spin-0 spec anywhere.  Markov
is the one case here where the collapse does not complete (2 pieces).
`fs_closed_form` honest-fails (`None`) off the acyclic case, which is the scope of
that *route*, not of the phenomenon.

### 9d. Benchmark: joint `F·S` against `S`-solving then `F`-solving

User, 2026-08-13: *"benchmark FS solving against S-solving followed by
F-solving"*.  `experiments/fs_builder_vs_s_then_f.py`, all three routes spec-free,
exact, and cone-truncated at the same degree; every route's `F_γ` checked against
the S-then-F route's before being timed.  At `D = 4`, ms per charge:

| quiver | N | `t_S` | `t_F`/γ | `S+F`/γ | joint/γ | closed/γ |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| pentagon | 6 | 4.0 | 0.2 | 4.2 | 1.5 | **0.7** |
| Kronecker-2 | 5 | 2.5 | 1.2 | 3.7 | 1.6 | **0.8** |
| Kronecker-3 | 3 | 2.5 | 5.0 | 7.4 | 1.7 | **0.7** |
| A3 | 4 | 15.2 | 0.2 | 15.4 | 3.2 | **1.8** |
| 3-cycle(1,1,1) | 2 | 45.6 | 0.3 | 45.9 | **7.0** | — |
| Markov | 2 | 34.1 | 2.4 | 36.4 | **9.3** | — |

**Neither route dominates, and the split is by regime rather than by quiver.**

* **One charge, cold.**  The joint build wins everywhere measured, 2.3× to 6.6×:
  S-then-F pays the whole `S` build to get one `F`.
* **Many charges off one quiver.**  S-then-F wins, and by more than the table's
  `amort` column shows — `N` is only 2–6 here so `t_S/N` still dominates, and the
  `N → ∞` limit is the `t_F` column itself: 0.2 ms at pentagon / A3 / 3-cycle
  against a 1.5–7.0 ms joint build.  `S` is built once and each further `F` is
  nearly free.
* **The exception is Kronecker-3**, where the `F`-solve is itself expensive
  (5.0 ms — a deep doubly-tropical interval) and the joint build wins ~3× even
  amortised.  So the crossover is set by the interval's depth, not by rank.
* **The closed form of §9c beats both wherever it applies** — 0.7–1.8 ms with no
  amortisation to do, up to 21× the cold S-then-F at Kronecker-3 — and
  honest-fails at 3-cycle / Markov.

So: the joint builder for a few charges or a deep interval, S-then-F for many
charges off one quiver, and the γ-dependent closed form whenever it is available.
The joint builder's structural advantages (no `S` input, no `σ⁻¹`, no support
window) are what it is *for*; on throughput alone it is not a replacement.

### 9b. The recursion as built

**The two moves are one alphabet.**  A BPS factor is fixed by a palindromic
multiplicity `Ω = Σ_s a_s χ_s`; an `F`-coefficient is a palindromic Laurent
polynomial, which the shipped solver peels in the `[n]_𝖖` basis.  These are the
same `Z`-basis of the palindromic Laurent polynomials:

    [n]_𝖖 = 𝖖^{−(n−1)} + ⋯ + 𝖖^{n−1} = χ_{(n−1)/2} .

The moves differ in *where* what they add lands, not in what it is: a BPS factor
at `γ'` enters through `S`, so it reaches `F·S` shifted by the quantum-torus
bracket and smeared by the `E_𝖖` tail `L = 𝖖/(1−𝖖²)`; an `F`-summand at `γ+γ'`
enters against `S_0 = 1`, bare and unshifted.

**Why the recursion closes.**  With `F = Σ_k c_k X_{γ+k}` over the cone in node
coordinates (`c_0 = 1`),

    [F·S]_{γ+k}  =  Σ_{k' ≤ k}  c_{k'} · 𝖖^{⟨γ+k', k−k'⟩} · S_{k−k'} ,

so at cone degree `d = deg k` exactly two unknowns of that degree appear: `c_k`
(at `k' = k`, against `S_0 = 1`) and `Ω_k` (at `k' = 0`, through `S_k`).  Every
other term has both factors of strictly smaller degree.  Same degree induction as
§3's, which is why the two recursions interleave rather than having to be
sequenced — and it is what "does not rely on `S`" buys: no `S` is ever an input,
and no `F`-support window is ever needed.

**The freedom is real, and naming it is the point.**  `F·S = X_γ + O(𝖖)`
constrains only the `𝖖^{≤0}` part, and a palindromic Laurent polynomial is
*determined by its non-positive part* — so for **any** `Ω` there is a unique `c`
completing the relation.  `Ω ≡ 0` gives `S = 1`, `F = X_γ`, which satisfies it.
So the relation alone pins neither object; what makes the build deterministic is
the one input the `S` builder already takes, `S`'s leading data.  Then

    S's leading data at k     forces  Ω_k     (`bps_factor_spectrum.forced_multiplicity`)
    F·S = X_γ + O(𝖖) at γ+k   forces  c_k     (palindromic completion of −[𝖖^{≤0}])

`FSBuilder(omega_policy=…)` exposes the choice for anyone who wants to search it
instead — the other axis beside §8's search over orderings.  The `Ω ≡ 0`
degenerate solution is pinned in the battery, so the caveat is measured rather
than asserted.

**Evidence, and what is NOT evidence.**  `verify_fs_leading` re-checks the
relation each `c_k` was solved from: a regression guard on the arithmetic, never
support for the construction — §7's A44 caveat applies verbatim.  *(It is
recomputed from the output `F` and `S` through the raw lattice pairing rather
than read back from the build's own accumulator: the read-back version was
vacuous in the strong sense — a corrupted bracket entered `c_k` and the stored
residual identically and cancelled, so the negative control passed on a broken
engine.  Caught by that control, which now measures the detection.)*

What is emergent:

* **agreement with the shipped solver.**  `BPSKAlgebra.F_qn` solves against a
  Nahm-expanded `S` over the enumerated doubly-tropical interval; no shared code
  path beyond exact `HabiroElement` arithmetic.
* **the support.**  This builder walks the whole cone and never sees the interval
  `[γ, −σ⁻¹γ]`, so `c_k = 0` outside it is an independent output.  Measured with
  the cutoff raised past the shipped support, which is where a builder that
  merely stopped in time would start emitting spurious coefficients — at
  Kronecker-3, `γ = (−1,1)`: a cone of 190 charges, nonzero on exactly the 34 the
  interval predicts.
* **order-independence of `F`** across placement orders whose ray *content*
  differs widely (2 to 13 rays at the same charge), matching the evidence class
  the `S` engine rests on.

**Measured (2026-08-13).**  `experiments/fs_builder_dictionary_sweep.py` over the
canonical BPS-quiver dictionary, ranks 1–4, 79 entries, a fixed charge spread
that includes negative charges (where `F` stops being a monomial):

| | |
|---|---:|
| charges where `F` agrees with `BPSKAlgebra.F_qn`, coefficient for coefficient | **535** |
| disagreements | **0** |
| of those, re-run with the cutoff 2 degrees past the shipped support | **475** |
| spurious coefficients outside the interval, in that wider window | **0** |

⚠ **The sweep is bounded and the bound is not small**: 71 further charges were
skipped entirely and 60 more had only the agreement half run, both for cone size
`> 250` points (cost is `≈ |cone| × |supp F|` exact Habiro products, and
`cutoff_needed` grows fast — Kronecker-3 at `γ = (−1,1)` alone wants degree 15).
Those are **not** passes and the script prints them as such.  This is a sample,
not the dictionary-wide `1108/1108` the `S` engine has.

**One thing NOT claimed.**  At Markov / N=2\* the joint builder agrees with the
shipped solver on every charge tried — but the shipped solver *works* there once
handed a ray-built `S`, so this is corroboration at a quiver with no finite
chamber, **not** new reach.  The reach the construction does add is structural:
no `S` input and no support window, so nothing has to know `σ⁻¹` before `F` is
built.
